column2: Open robot_otak.ino. Fill in the CONFIGURATION section: WiFi, token, chat ID, Gemini API key, Groq API key (may be empty, but recommended as a backup), and leave KAMERA_ALAMAT empty. The robot finds the camera by itself and follows it even when the camera IP changes: the camera (latest eye code) broadcasts its address on the WiFi every 30 seconds, and if the camera does not answer, the robot looks up robotcam.local again. Putting an IP in KAMERA_ALAMAT only speeds up the first search.
OK to lock in The filled-in robot_otak.ino (WiFi, token, chat ID, API key, robot name). The touch calibration is stored on the S3.

Photo fails: is the camera on and on the same WiFi as the brain? Is the /stream tab in the browser closed? The brain Serial Monitor prints [kamera] alamat ... -> ... every time the camera address changes. If it never appears, upload the latest eye code again (over USB) so the camera broadcasts its address.

The flashlight says "Kamera tidak menjawab" (camera not answering): the ESP32-CAM is not on yet or not connected to the same WiFi. The robot looks for the camera again every minute and every time the camera does not answer. The flash LED is dimmed on purpose in the eye code (analogWrite 60) so it does not overheat; raise the number in robot_mata.ino if it is too dim, 255 at most, and do not keep it on for long at that value.
